doc.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001

title: Harmony over race or mission
summary: He insists harmonic opening of the American ear, not race or artistic mission, changed jazz.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: And it allowed, did it allow for those songs for instance that don’t start on the one chord.
Is that part of what you’re talking about?
No I’m just talking about how music was harmonized.
The decline of the dominant seventh and its replacement by suspended introductory harmony.
A lot more than race or some kind of purposeful artistic mission. I mean it was the opening up of the American ear by Gershwin, Cole Porter, that’s it. I mean that’s it. That’s the way I feel.

Okay. Great statement. It’s going to give me some food for thought for sure. Yeah there’s an awful lot of statements made about what jazz players were intending to do and their role in society and all that, and maybe it’s not that complicated.
It’s like joining a lodge, a secret handshake, everybody knows it’s like a two chord.
I feel like I just got a little secret of life here.
